1	# The Assistant
2	
3	The Assistant is a conversation with Claude, built into the inspector of every editor window. You ask in plain words ("trim the pauses out of the interview", "put a title over the first five seconds", "what is under the playhead?"), and it reads and edits the window's project with the same tools an agent uses over MCP. You watch each change land, and each one is its own undo step. It runs on your own Anthropic API key, so Anthropic bills its usage to your account. Frame Job shows its own estimate of what each turn and each month costs.
4	
5	## Setting it up
6	
7	Open **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (⌘,). The **Assistant** section is second, under MCP and above Transcription. The ⓘ beside its heading explains what is sent, what it costs and what the chat settings do.
8	
9	| Control | What it does | Default |
10	|---|---|---|
11	| **Anthropic API key:** | A secure field, with the placeholder "Paste your key". Paste the key and click **Save** (or press Return in the field). The field empties, and from then on a saved key shows only as a fixed-length mask. It is never shown again. **Remove** deletes the saved key and is enabled only while one is saved. | none |
12	| **Model:** | The Claude model the assistant uses. Leave it blank to use the default. A change takes effect when you press Return or leave the field, and only a change to a different model ends conversations: retyping the current model, or blanking the field while the default is in use, changes nothing. | `claude-opus-5-5` |
13	| **Compact when context reaches … tokens** | When on, a long conversation is replaced by a summary at the end of the first turn that passes the threshold (see [Long conversations](#long-conversations-the-context-meter-and-compaction)). The field accepts 20,000 to 900,000 and is enabled only while the box is checked. | on, 300,000 |
14	| **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** | Lets Anthropic drop old tool results from what the model sees. | off |
15	
16	Under the controls, a status line reports the key's state: "No API key is set." (when neither a saved key nor the environment provides one), "Key saved." or "Key removed.". If the key file cannot be written or removed, the status line shows the file error instead, and nothing changes. Clicking **Save** with an empty field beeps. A threshold outside the range also beeps, and the field goes back to the stored value.
17	
18	**What ends a conversation.** A conversation keeps the key and model it started with. Saving or removing the key, or changing the model to a different one, ends the conversation in every open window. The transcript stays and gets a note: "The API key changed; the next message starts a new conversation." or "The model is now … ; the next message starts a new conversation.". The two chat settings apply without Save and without ending anything. A new compaction threshold applies at the end of the current turn, and a change to clearing applies from the next message.
19	
20	### Where the key is kept
21	
22	A saved key is stored in a file named `anthropic-key` in `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`, which only your user account can read. It goes to the assistant's helper process when a conversation starts and nowhere else. No tool reads or writes the key, the model or the chat settings, so an agent connected over MCP cannot see or change them.
23	
24	If no key is saved, Frame Job uses the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable instead. In practice that only applies when Frame Job is launched from a shell that sets the variable. A saved key always takes precedence.
25	
26	## Opening the Assistant
27	
28	The Assistant is the fifth tab of the inspector, after Clip, Media, Document and Transcript. **View ▸ Assistant** (⌃⌘A) shows the inspector if it was hidden, switches to the Assistant tab and puts the cursor in the message field.
29	
30	From top to bottom, the tab has:
31	
32	1. **Context**: the context meter, with **Clear** (↺, "Clear the conversation") at its right end.
33	2. **Spend**: what this conversation has cost so far.
34	3. **The transcript.**
35	4. **The ask-first row**, shown only while the assistant is waiting for your permission.
36	5. **The message field and Send.**
37	
38	Without a key, the message field is replaced by "Add your Anthropic API key in Settings to use the assistant." and an **Open Settings…** button. **View ▸ Assistant** stays enabled with no key, so the tab can say this; saving the key in Settings brings the message field back at once. If a conversation is started without a key anyway (an agent's `assistant_send`), it fails with "No Anthropic API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant."
39	
40	The tab doesn't switch away on its own while you work in it. The assistant's own edits change the selection without moving you to the Clip tab. Clicking a clip in the timeline or on the canvas still shows the Clip tab, as it always does.
41	
42	## Sending a message
43	
44	Type in the field ("Ask about or edit this project…") and press Return or click **Send**. The field starts one line high and grows to five lines as you type. Past five lines it scrolls.
45	
46	| Key | In the message field |
47	|---|---|
48	| Return or keypad Enter | Sends the message and gives the keys back to the editor, so Space plays while the assistant works. While the assistant is working or waiting for an answer, it beeps instead and the field keeps the keys. |
49	| ⇧Return, ⌘Return, ⌥Return, ⌃Return | Starts a new line |
50	| Tab, ⇧Tab | Gives the keys back to the editor. With Full Keyboard Access on, moves focus to the next or previous control |
51	| ⌘Z, ⇧⌘Z | Undoes or redoes your typing. Typing never lands on the project's undo stack. |
52	
53	The field empties once the message is sent. If the conversation cannot start (for example, the key was removed), the reason appears in red in the transcript and your text stays in the field.
54	
55	While a turn runs, **Send** reads **Stop**. See [Stopping a turn](#stopping-a-turn).
56	
57	### What each message carries
58	
59	Each message you send starts with a short block describing your window at the moment you pressed Send:
60	
61	- the project's name, and its path (or "never saved")
62	- the nest open in the window, if any (otherwise the timeline)
63	- the playhead, in ticks and in seconds
64	- the selected clip ids
65	
66	So "split this clip at the playhead" or "make the selected titles bigger" mean what you'd expect. The block isn't updated during the assistant's turn. After its own edits, the assistant reads the project again.
67	
68	## The transcript
69	
70	The transcript is one block of text. You can select across entries and copy it as plain text. It scrolls to the newest line as the reply arrives.
71	
72	| What you see | Style |
73	|---|---|
74	| Your message | Semibold |
75	| The assistant's reply, streamed as it is written | Regular |
76	| Its working notes between tool calls | Small, faint |
77	| One line per tool call: the tool's name and its arguments, e.g. `split (at: 96000, clips: [12])` (first 70 characters) | Small monospace |
78	| `failed: …` for a tool call that was refused, with the reason | Small monospace |
79	| `Allowed: …` / `Declined: …` for each permission question, or `Declined (stop): …`, `Declined (close): …` or `Declined (helper): …` when it was declined by Stop, by closing the window or by the helper stopping | Small monospace |
80	| Compaction and clearing notes, and notes about key, model or spend-ledger problems | Small monospace |
81	| `Cost: …` at the end of each turn | Small monospace |
82	| Errors | Red |
83	
84	Errors you may see:
85	
86	- "API error *status*: *message*": Anthropic refused or failed the request (a bad key, a rate limit, an outage). Rate limits, outages and connection failures are retried up to three times before this appears. A bad key fails at once.
87	- "The reply was cut off at the output limit."
88	- "The model declined this request."
89	- "The assistant helper stopped. Clear the conversation to start a new one."
90	
91	If the helper stops, a waiting question is declined. Your next message starts a new conversation under the old transcript, and the Spend row carries on from where it was. Click **Clear** to start clean.
92	
93	If a response's cost cannot be written to the spend ledger, the transcript notes it once per conversation: "The spend ledger *path* could not be written: *reason*." That response is then missing from the month's total in Settings.
94	
95	The assistant works for up to 30 rounds of tool calls in one turn, then stops.
96	
97	**Clear** (↺) ends the conversation, empties the transcript and resets the Spend row and the meter. The meter keeps the model's window size, so it reads "0 of *L* tokens · 0%" until the next response. Your next message starts a fresh conversation. Closing the window also ends its conversation. Conversations aren't saved with the project, and each window has its own.
98	
99	## What the assistant can do
100	
101	The assistant has the same tools an agent has over MCP (see [MCP](mcp.md)), with a few exceptions listed below. It can:
102	
103	- open, create and save projects, move the playhead, set the in and out range, change the selection, and enter or leave a nest
104	- add, remove, reorder and set tracks; add and edit markers; change the canvas
105	- import, relink and remove media, copy it into the project (it asks first), and set a media's camera log
106	- place media, text, shapes, backgrounds, adjustment clips and graphics; insert, overwrite, paste and duplicate
107	- move, trim, split, slip, roll, rate-stretch, ripple-delete, lift, insert time and close gaps; detach audio and attach it again, and make J- and L-cuts
108	- nest clips, or take a nest apart
109	- set speed, reverse, freeze frames and add speed ramps (see [Speed](speed.md))
110	- change how a clip looks and sounds, including transitions, actions and zooms; rename a clip, hide or mute it, and paste attributes
111	- import captions, transcribe on this Mac, read a clip's timed words, and export captions
112	- find silences and filler words, normalize loudness and synchronize audio
113	- write, place and change graphics modules; import fonts and assets; rename, delete or restore a module
114	- export, check an export's progress, or cancel it
115	- render a frame of the timeline to look at the result, before and after a visual edit
116	
117	Every edit is one undo step on the project, the same as your own. A turn isn't grouped: each edit is its own step, so a turn that made ten edits takes ten Undos, and **Edit ▸ Undo** names each step after its edit, as it does for an agent's call over MCP. **Edit ▸ Undo** (⌘Z) outside the message field takes back the assistant's last change. You can also ask the assistant to undo.
118	
119	**How it behaves.** Its replies are short, a sentence or two, and don't repeat what the tool lines already show. It writes or restyles captions only when you ask. It renders a frame to look before and after a visual edit. The model runs at medium effort with thinking on, and the faint working notes between tool calls are its thinking updates.
120	
121	The assistant works only on its own window's project. A tool call that names another project is refused.
122	
123	**Cutting words.** Ask it to take out filler words and it finds them and cuts them in one step, but only in media that already have a cloud transcript made with filler words (by **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**). The assistant can't upload audio to make one, so in other media it cuts nothing (the search reports which media have no such transcript). Ask it to remove a false start and it reads the clip's words and their times (from the media's cached transcript, or from this Mac's own speech recogniser, never the network), says which words it will cut, then cuts them as one undo step. It removes a false start only when you ask, because deciding what was a false start is a judgement call. See [Clean-up tools](cleanup-tools.md).
124	
125	### Tools it will not call
126	
127	`record_screen`, `close_project` and `transcribe_for_fillers` are removed from what the assistant can see. `transcribe` stays available for transcribing on this Mac, and only a call with the cloud engine (AssemblyAI) is refused. All four are refused if the assistant calls them anyway, and the call shows in the transcript as a `failed:` line: "*tool* is not available to the assistant: *reason*" (for the cloud case, `transcribe with engine "assemblyai" is not available to the assistant: …`). The reason names the menu item to use instead.
128	
129	| Tool | Why | Do it yourself with |
130	|---|---|---|
131	| `record_screen` | Recording needs a person at the Record button. | **File ▸ New Recording…** (⌥⌘N) |
132	| `close_project` | Closing the project would close the window the conversation lives in. | **File ▸ Close** (⌘W) |
133	| `transcribe` with the cloud engine (AssemblyAI) | Audio leaves the machine only when you choose it, with the price in front of you. | **File ▸ Generate Captions…** |
134	| `transcribe_for_fillers` | The same: it uploads audio to the cloud. | **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…** |
135	
136	### Tools it asks about first
137	
138	Five tools ask first: `export`, `export_captions`, `save_project`, `consolidate_media` and `export_graphic`; a sixth, `new_project_from_range`, asks only when it names a `path` (without one it opens an untitled project and writes no package); and a seventh, `make_vertical_version`, asks only when it names a `path` too. Before each one runs, the tab shows the ask-first row, "The assistant asks first:", with a sentence that says what will happen, and **Allow** and **Deny** buttons:
139	
140	| Tool | The question reads |
141	|---|---|
142	| `export` | "export writes *path*", or "export REPLACES *path*" when a file is already there |
143	| `export_captions` | "export_captions writes *path*" (or REPLACES) |
144	| `save_project` | "save_project writes *path*" (or REPLACES); "save_project writes a file" when no path is known |
145	| `consolidate_media` | "consolidate_media copies every referenced file into *package*/media", or "… into the project's package" when the project has never been saved |
146	| `new_project_from_range` | "new_project_from_range writes *path*", `.framejob` added when missing (only with a `path`) |
147	| `make_vertical_version` | "make_vertical_version writes *path*", `.framejob` added when missing (only with a `path`) |
148	
149	A `~` in the path is expanded before the question is asked, so the sentence shows the full path.
150	
151	Other tools the assistant can call write files without asking: `render_frame` writes a PNG (to a temporary file, or to a path the model names), and `write_graphic`, `import_graphic_font` and `import_graphic_asset` write graphics modules, fonts and assets into the project's package.
152	
153	While a question waits, the **Assistant** tab title shows a small dot, whichever inspector tab you are on. Answer with a click: Return never answers a question. Nothing runs until you click **Allow**. **Deny** tells the assistant you declined, and it won't retry that call in the same turn unless you ask. Stopping the turn, closing the window or the helper stopping each count as a decline. Other windows' assistants and agents over MCP keep working while one window waits for an answer.
154	
155	### While you are dragging
156	
157	If one of the assistant's tool calls arrives while you are in the middle of a drag (on the timeline, the canvas or an inspector slider), it waits until you release the mouse. Then it runs as its own undo step, after yours, so your drag never undoes the assistant's change or mixes with it. The same applies to agents over MCP.
158	
159	The assistant's tool calls and MCP agents' calls take turns, one at a time, and each window's calls run in order. While a window waits for your **Allow** or **Deny**, MCP agents and other windows keep working.
160	
161	### Stopping a turn
162	
163	Click **Stop** (the Send button while a turn runs). Stop:
164	
165	- ends the request to Anthropic
166	- declines a question that is waiting
167	- answers every tool call that has not started yet with "Cancelled by the user."
168	- cancels an on-device transcription or transcript read that is running. Any other tool call that has already started is allowed to finish.
169	
170	An export is handed to the Export Queue as soon as it starts, so Stop doesn't reach it. Cancel it in the Export Queue, or ask the assistant to cancel it. See [Export](export.md).
171	
172	## Long conversations: the context meter and compaction
173	
174	The **Context** meter shows how much of the model's context window the conversation is using, as of the last response:
175	
176	- "Nothing reported yet" before the first response
177	- "*N* of *L* tokens · *P*%" once the model's window is known (shortened to "*N* / *L* · *P*%" or "*P*%" when the inspector is narrow; the tooltip always has the full figure)
178	- "*N* tokens (window size unknown)" if Anthropic did not report the window size
179	
180	The bar under the figure fills in the accent colour and turns red past 80%.
181	
182	**Compaction.** With **Compact when context reaches** on, the conversation is summarised at the end of the first turn that passes the threshold, never in the middle of a turn. The summary keeps what you asked for and your stated preferences, the project and the clips, tracks, markers and media involved, the edits made and undone, and what is still open. The transcript notes "Compacting the conversation (*N* tokens)…" and then "Compacted: *N* → about *M* tokens. Earlier renders are gone; the assistant re-renders when it needs to look.". If no summary comes back, the note says compaction didn't finish and that it will try again after the next turn. The summary request is priced like any other response.
183	
184	With compaction off, a conversation grows until it fills the model's window, and requests then fail until you click **Clear**.
185	
186	**Clearing old tool results.** With **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** on, Anthropic may drop older tool results from what the model sees once the conversation passes 150,000 tokens. It keeps the five most recent, clears at least 50,000 tokens at a time, and can happen mid-turn. Each clearing adds a note, "Cleared *N* old tool results (*M* tokens) from the model's view.", and costs a fresh prompt-cache write. The model may have to fetch something again after a clearing.
187	
188	## What it costs
189	
190	Every response is priced by Frame Job from LiteLLM's published Anthropic prices. All the figures below are **Frame Job's own estimate**. The Anthropic Console shows what your account was actually billed.
191	
192	### Per turn
193	
194	Each turn ends with a line in the transcript:
195	
196	`Cost: $0.0182 · Frame Job's estimate at LiteLLM prices (cached 2026-10-25)`
197	
198	The part in brackets names the price table and its date: "bundled table of …" (the copy built into the app), "cached …" or "fetched …" (a copy Frame Job refreshes at most once a day). If a refresh failed, the line adds "not refreshed:" and the reason.
199	
200	- A response that could not be priced shows as "unknown (*reason*)", never $0, followed by "at least" the part that could be priced.
201	- A response cut short by Stop or an error is priced from what had arrived, as "at least $… (a response was cut short)".
202	- Amounts are shown to four decimal places. A tiny positive amount reads "under $0.0001".
203	
204	### Per conversation
205	
206	The tab's **Spend** row adds up the conversation's turns since the last **Clear**, or since a key or model change ended the conversation:
207	
208	- "Nothing yet" before the first response
209	- "$0.0532 · Frame Job's estimate"
210	- "at least $… · Frame Job's estimate" when a response was cut short or could not be priced (shortened to "≥$…" when narrow)
211	- "under $0.0001 · Frame Job's estimate" for a tiny positive amount (shortened to "<$0.0001" when narrow)
212	- "unknown · Frame Job's estimate" when nothing could be priced
213	
214	Hovering the figure shows "What this conversation's responses cost at LiteLLM prices, as Frame Job estimates it. The Anthropic Console shows what your account was billed."
215	
216	### Per month
217	
218	Under the buttons in **Settings ▸ Assistant**, a line totals the current calendar month in UTC, for example "October 2026 (UTC): $1.24 over 87 responses.". Variants report "Nothing recorded in …", responses that could not be priced, and ledger lines that could not be read. Totals are rounded to the cent, and a tiny positive amount reads "under $0.01". While the ledger is being read the line says "Reading the spend ledger…", and if it cannot be read, "The spend ledger could not be read: *reason*.". The line refreshes when Settings opens and after each response while Settings is visible. Under it, a faint note says: "Frame Job's own estimate at LiteLLM prices, from its spend ledger. The Anthropic Console shows what your account was billed."
219	
220	The figures come from a spend ledger, `spend.jsonl` in `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`, with one line per response: the time, the model, the token counts and the dollars. It never records your key or the conversation's content.
221	
222	## Privacy: what leaves your Mac
223	
224	When you use the assistant, these go to Anthropic, under your key:
225	
226	- your messages, and the context block in front of each one (the project's name and path, the open nest, the playhead, the selection)
227	- what the tools answer: the project's details as JSON (including media file paths), clip transcripts it reads, refusals and other results
228	- the frames it renders to look at the picture
229	
230	Frame Job doesn't send any of this anywhere else. Audio never goes to the cloud transcriber from the assistant (see [Tools it will not call](#tools-it-will-not-call)). The assistant asks before it exports a movie or captions, saves the project, or consolidates media; other tools can still write files without asking (a rendered frame's PNG, and graphics modules, fonts and assets in the project's package). Once a day at most, the helper downloads LiteLLM's public price table from GitHub. That request carries no key and no project data.
231	
232	Everything else stays on your Mac: the key file, the spend ledger and the cached price table, `anthropic-prices.json`, all in `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`. The conversation itself is kept in memory only, and goes when you clear it or close the window.
233	
234	## Limits
235	
236	- The assistant works only on the project in its own window, and each window has its own conversation.
237	- It needs your own Anthropic API key. There is no Frame Job account or relay.
238	- It can't record the screen, close its window's project, or send audio to the cloud transcriber.
239	- A tool call that arrives during a drag waits until you release the mouse.
240	- Stop doesn't cancel an export that has already been queued.
241	- With compaction off, a long conversation eventually fails until you **Clear** it.
242	- Changing the key or the model ends every window's conversation.
243	
244	*Agents:* none. The Assistant is the person's own conversation, and its settings are deliberately out of reach of any tool. An agent drives the same tools directly over [MCP](mcp.md), and is never asked first or refused by the assistant's rules above.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is

traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

3	/// The Assistant tab's composer (spec §11 AI-17): a plain-text view that
4	/// grows from one line to five inside `AssistantComposerField`.
5	///
6	/// **Keys.** A bare Return or keypad Enter is `onReturn` (the view sends
7	/// while idle and beeps otherwise — never an answer); Return with ⇧, ⌘, ⌥ or
8	/// ⌃ inserts "\n", K-2's rule through the same `TextEditKey.route`, and
9	/// nothing is routed while an input method has marked text. Tab and ⇧Tab
10	/// never type a tab: in the editor window `TextFocus` takes them first and
11	/// hands the keys back to the editor (spec §11 K-4), as a Return that sends
12	/// does (`AssistantView.send`); with Full Keyboard Access on they reach
13	/// here and move focus along the key-view loop.
14	///
15	/// **Undo is its own.** An editable text view takes its undo manager from
16	/// the window, and an editor window's IS the document's, so typing would
17	/// land on the project's stack. The override hands AppKit `ownUndoManager`
18	/// instead: ⌘Z here undoes typing, and typing never touches the document's
19	/// stack, its dirty state or `registerUndo`'s grouping (AI-10, app/CLAUDE.md's
20	/// Undo). A programmatic `string` (a send, the dev tools' pane path) drops
21	/// that history. The window's own `undo:` reads the WINDOW's manager, not the
22	/// first responder's (measured: `assistant_tab_probe` P11), so the composer
23	/// answers `undo:` and `redo:` itself, over the same manager.
24	final class AssistantComposerTextView: NSTextView {
25	    var placeholder: String = "" {
26	        didSet {
27	            setAccessibilityPlaceholderValue(placeholder)
28	            needsDisplay = true
29	        }
30	    }
31	    /// A bare Return or keypad Enter.
32	    var onReturn: (() -> Void)?
33	    /// Every change to the string, typed or set; the field refits.
34	    var onChange: (() -> Void)?
35	    private let ownUndoManager = UndoManager()
36	
37	    override var undoManager: UndoManager? { ownUndoManager }
38	
39	    override var string: String {
40	        didSet {
41	            ownUndoManager.removeAllActions()
42	            onChange?()
43	            needsDisplay = true
44	        }
45	    }
46	
47	    @objc func undo(_ sender: Any?) {
48	        ownUndoManager.undo()
49	    }
50	
51	    @objc func redo(_ sender: Any?) {
52	        ownUndoManager.redo()
53	    }
54	
55	    override func validateUserInterfaceItem(_ item: NSValidatedUserInterfaceItem) -> Bool {
56	        switch item.action {
57	        case #selector(undo(_:)):
58	            (item as? NSMenuItem)?.title = ownUndoManager.undoMenuItemTitle
59	            return ownUndoManager.canUndo
60	        case #selector(redo(_:)):
61	            (item as? NSMenuItem)?.title = ownUndoManager.redoMenuItemTitle
62	            return ownUndoManager.canRedo
63	        default:
64	            return super.validateUserInterfaceItem(item)
65	        }
66	    }
67	
68	    override func keyDown(with event: NSEvent) {
69	        switch TextEditKey.route(event, hasMarkedText: hasMarkedText()) {
70	        case .apply: onReturn?()
71	        case .newline: insertNewline(nil)
72	        case .escape, nil: super.keyDown(with: event)
73	        }
74	    }
75	
76	    override func insertTab(_ sender: Any?) {
77	        window?.selectNextKeyView(sender)
78	    }
79	
80	    override func insertBacktab(_ sender: Any?) {
81	        window?.selectPreviousKeyView(sender)
82	    }
83	
84	    override func didChangeText() {
85	        super.didChangeText()
86	        onChange?()
87	        needsDisplay = true
88	    }
89	
90	    /// Where the placeholder is drawn: one line high, at the text's origin.
91	    var placeholderRect: NSRect {
92	        let padding = textContainer?.lineFragmentPadding ?? 0
93	        let origin = textContainerOrigin
94	        let width = max(bounds.width - origin.x * 2 - padding * 2, 0)
95	        let height = AssistantComposerField.lineHeight(font ?? DS.sans(12))
96	        return NSRect(x: origin.x + padding, y: origin.y, width: width, height: height)
97	    }
98	
99	    override func draw(_ dirtyRect: NSRect) {
100	        super.draw(dirtyRect)
101	        guard string.isEmpty, !placeholder.isEmpty else { return }
102	        let attributes: [NSAttributedString.Key: Any] = [
103	            .font: font ?? DS.sans(12), .foregroundColor: NSColor.placeholderTextColor,
104	        ]
105	        (placeholder as NSString).draw(
106	            with: placeholderRect, options: [.usesLineFragmentOrigin, .truncatesLastVisibleLine],
107	            attributes: attributes)
108	    }
109	}
110	
111	/// The composer's frame: DSField's square 1 pt border round a scroll view
112	/// whose text view is `AssistantComposerTextView`. 26 pt for one line, one
113	/// line height more per further line up to `maxLines`; past that the height
114	/// holds and the text scrolls. It refits on every change to the string and
115	/// on any width change.
116	final class AssistantComposerField: NSScrollView {
117	    static let maxLines = 5
118	    static let oneLineHeight: CGFloat = 26
119	    let textView: AssistantComposerTextView
120	    private var height: NSLayoutConstraint?
121	    private var fittedWidth: CGFloat = -1
122	
123	    init() {
124	        textView = AssistantComposerTextView(usingTextLayoutManager: false)
125	        super.init(frame: .zero)
126	        hasVerticalScroller = true
127	        hasHorizontalScroller = false
128	        autohidesScrollers = true
129	        borderType = .noBorder
130	        drawsBackground = true
131	        backgroundColor = .textBackgroundColor
132	        wantsLayer = true
133	        layer?.borderWidth = 1
134	        layer?.cornerRadius = DS.fieldRadius
135	        refreshBorder()
136	
137	        let font = DS.sans(12)
138	        textView.isRichText = false
139	        textView.allowsUndo = true
140	        textView.font = font
141	        textView.textColor = DS.textStrong
142	        textView.insertionPointColor = DS.textStrong
143	        textView.drawsBackground = true
144	        textView.backgroundColor = .textBackgroundColor
145	        textView.typingAttributes = [.font: font, .foregroundColor: DS.textStrong]
146	        let lineHeight = Self.lineHeight(font)
147	        textView.textContainer?.lineFragmentPadding = 4
148	        textView.textContainerInset = NSSize(
149	            width: 2, height: max((Self.oneLineHeight - lineHeight) / 2, 0))
150	        textView.textContainer?.widthTracksTextView = true
151	        textView.isVerticallyResizable = true
152	        textView.isHorizontallyResizable = false
153	        textView.minSize = .zero
154	        textView.maxSize = NSSize(
155	            width: CGFloat.greatestFiniteMagnitude, height: CGFloat.greatestFiniteMagnitude)
156	        textView.autoresizingMask = [.width]
157	        textView.frame = NSRect(origin: .zero, size: contentSize)
158	        textView.onChange = { [weak self] in self?.fit() }
159	        documentView = textView
160	
161	        let constraint = heightAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: Self.oneLineHeight)
162	        constraint.isActive = true
163	        height = constraint
164	    }
165	
166	    @available(*, unavailable)
167	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
168	        fatalError("AssistantComposerField does not support NSCoder")
169	    }
170	
171	    override func layout() {
172	        super.layout()
173	        guard bounds.width != fittedWidth else { return }
174	        fittedWidth = bounds.width
175	        fit()
176	    }
177	
178	    override func viewDidChangeEffectiveAppearance() {
179	        super.viewDidChangeEffectiveAppearance()
180	        refreshBorder()
181	    }
182	
183	    /// The height for the string's line count, capped at `maxLines`.
184	    func fit() {
185	        guard let layout = textView.layoutManager, let container = textView.textContainer
186	        else { return }
187	        let lineHeight = Self.lineHeight(textView.font ?? DS.sans(12))
188	        layout.ensureLayout(for: container)
189	        let used = layout.usedRect(for: container).height
190	        let lines = max(1, Int((used / lineHeight).rounded()))
191	        let shown = CGFloat(min(lines, Self.maxLines))
192	        let wanted = Self.oneLineHeight + (shown - 1) * lineHeight
193	        textView.sizeToFit()
194	        if height?.constant != wanted { height?.constant = wanted }
195	    }
196	
197	    static func lineHeight(_ font: NSFont) -> CGFloat {
198	        NSLayoutManager().defaultLineHeight(for: font)
199	    }
200	
201	    private func refreshBorder() {
202	        effectiveAppearance.performAsCurrentDrawingAppearance {
203	            layer?.borderColor = DS.borderStrong.cgColor
204	        }
205	    }
206	}

16	/// `askOnlyWith` narrows an ask-first row to calls carrying that argument
17	/// (`new_project_from_range` asks only when it names `path`, CJ-52); declared
18	/// last, with a default, so every other row's init is unchanged.

20	    let tool: String
21	    let rule: AssistantToolRule
22	    let onlyWith: (key: String, value: String)?
23	    let reason: String

25	}

32	    let exists: Bool
33

35	    /// there (A0 E2: `export` replaces without asking), "<tool> writes a file"
36	    /// with no path; `consolidate_media` says what it copies, and where.

38	        if tool == "consolidate_media" {

40	                + (path ?? "the project's package")
41	        }

45	}

47	enum AssistantToolTable {
48	    /// The product tools the table names. The dev tools are withheld too, by
49	    /// `row(for:)`, from `AgentServer.devToolNames`, so a new dev tool needs no
50	    /// row here.
51	    static let rows: [AssistantToolRow] = [
52	        AssistantToolRow(
53	            tool: "record_screen", rule: .withheld, onlyWith: nil,
54	            reason: "Recording is a person at the Record button (File ▸ New Recording…)."),
55	        AssistantToolRow(
56	            tool: "close_project", rule: .withheld, onlyWith: nil,
57	            reason: "Closing a project closes the window this conversation lives in (AI-5); the "
58	                + "person closes it with File ▸ Close (⌘W)."),
59	        AssistantToolRow(
60	            tool: "transcribe", rule: .withheld, onlyWith: (key: "engine", value: "assemblyai"),
61	            reason: "Audio leaves the machine only by name, with the price in front of the "
62	                + "person (spec §11 R6-2). Use File ▸ Generate Captions…, which shows what is "
63	                + "uploaded and what it costs."),
64	        AssistantToolRow(
65	            tool: "transcribe_for_fillers", rule: .withheld, onlyWith: nil,
66	            reason: "Audio leaves the machine only by name, with the price in front of the "
67	                + "person (spec §11 R6-2). Use Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…, which shows what is "
68	                + "uploaded and what it costs."),
69	        AssistantToolRow(
70	            tool: "export", rule: .askFirst, onlyWith: nil,
71	            reason: "It writes a movie where the model chose, replacing any file already there "
72	                + "(A0 E2)."),
73	        AssistantToolRow(
74	            tool: "export_captions", rule: .askFirst, onlyWith: nil,
75	            reason: "It writes a caption file."),
76	        AssistantToolRow(
77	            tool: "save_project", rule: .askFirst, onlyWith: nil,
78	            reason: "It writes the package."),
79	        AssistantToolRow(
80	            tool: "consolidate_media", rule: .askFirst, onlyWith: nil,
81	            reason: "It copies every referenced file into the package."),
82	        AssistantToolRow(
83	            tool: "export_graphic", rule: .askFirst, onlyWith: nil,
84	            reason: "It writes a .fjgraphic package where the model chose, replacing any file "
85	                + "already there."),
86	        AssistantToolRow(
87	            tool: "new_project_from_range", rule: .askFirst, onlyWith: nil,
88	            reason: "It writes a project package where the model chose, when the call names a "
89	                + "path.",
90	            askOnlyWith: "path"),
91	        AssistantToolRow(
92	            tool: "make_vertical_version", rule: .askFirst, onlyWith: nil,
93	            reason: "It writes a project package where the model chose, when the call names a "
94	                + "path.",
95	            askOnlyWith: "path"),
96	    ]
97	
98	    static let devToolReason =
99	        "a developer tool (spec §11 V-1): Distribution has none, and the assistant sees one "
100	        + "catalog in both builds."
101	
102	    /// The row governing `tool`: every dev tool is withheld (V-1), else the
103	    /// table's own row, else nil (the tool is the assistant's to call).
104	    static func row(for tool: String) -> AssistantToolRow? {
105	        if AgentServer.devToolNames.contains(tool) {
106	            return AssistantToolRow(
107	                tool: tool, rule: .withheld, onlyWith: nil, reason: devToolReason)
108	        }
109	        return rows.first { $0.tool == tool }
110	    }
111	
112	    /// The lane's refusal of a withheld call, or nil. A conditional row
113	    /// refuses only a call carrying its argument, and names it.
114	    static func refusal(tool: String, arguments: [String: Any]) -> String? {
115	        guard let entry = row(for: tool), entry.rule == .withheld else { return nil }
116	        var name = tool
117	        if let only = entry.onlyWith {
118	            guard arguments[only.key] as? String == only.value else { return nil }
119	            name = "\(tool) with \(only.key) \"\(only.value)\""
120	        }
121	        return "\(name) is not available to the assistant: \(entry.reason)"
122	    }
123	
124	    /// The question an ask-first call puts to the person, or nil for any other
125	    /// tool, and for an ask-first row's call without its `askOnlyWith`
126	    /// argument, which the lane then runs unasked. Main only: it reads the
127	    /// document and the file system.
128	    static func question(
129	        tool: String, arguments: [String: Any], document: ProjectDocument
130	    ) -> AssistantQuestion? {
131	        assert(Thread.isMainThread)
132	        guard let entry = row(for: tool), entry.rule == .askFirst else { return nil }
133	        if let key = entry.askOnlyWith, arguments[key] == nil { return nil }
134	        let given = (arguments["path"] as? String).map { ($0 as NSString).expandingTildeInPath }
135	        let path: String?
136	        switch tool {
137	        case "save_project":
138	            // Never `importSourceURL`: that is the movie, not where a save writes.
139	            path = given ?? document.fileURL?.path
140	        case "consolidate_media":
141	            path = document.fileURL.map { "\($0.path)/media" }
142	        case "export_graphic":
143	            // Where the tool will write: `.fjgraphic` added as `destinationURL` adds it.
144	            path = given.map {
145	                AgentServer.destinationURL($0, extension: GraphicPackage.fileExtension).path
146	            }
147	        case "new_project_from_range", "make_vertical_version":
148	            // Where the tool will write: `.framejob` added as `destinationURL` adds it.
149	            path = given.map {
150	                AgentServer.destinationURL($0, extension: ProjectDocument.projectFileExtension)
151	                    .path
152	            }
153	        default:
154	            path = given
155	        }
156	        let exists = path.map { FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: $0) } ?? false
157	        return AssistantQuestion(tool: tool, path: path, exists: exists)
158	    }
159	
160	    /// The catalog the assistant is handed: `tools` less every tool withheld
161	    /// outright. A conditional row (`transcribe`) keeps its tool, and the lane
162	    /// refuses the call it names.
163	    static func assistantCatalog(_ tools: [[String: Any]]) -> [[String: Any]] {
164	        tools.filter { tool in
165	            guard let name = tool["name"] as? String, let entry = row(for: name) else {
166	                return true
167	            }
168	            return !(entry.rule == .withheld && entry.onlyWith == nil)
169	        }
170	    }
171	}

1	# The Assistant
2	
3	The Assistant is a conversation with Claude, built into the inspector of every editor window. You ask in plain words ("trim the pauses out of the interview", "put a title over the first five seconds", "what is under the playhead?"), and it reads and edits the window's project with the same tools an agent uses over MCP. You watch each change land, and each one is its own undo step. It runs on your own Anthropic API key, so Anthropic bills its usage to your account. Frame Job shows its own estimate of what each turn and each month costs.
4	
5	## Setting it up
6	
7	Open **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (⌘,). The **Assistant** section is second, under MCP and above Transcription. The ⓘ beside its heading explains what is sent, what it costs and what the chat settings do.
8	
9	| Control | What it does | Default |
10	|---|---|---|
11	| **Anthropic API key:** | A secure field, with the placeholder "Paste your key". Paste the key and click **Save** (or press Return in the field). The field empties, and from then on a saved key shows only as a fixed-length mask. It is never shown again. **Remove** deletes the saved key and is enabled only while one is saved. | none |
12	| **Model:** | The Claude model the assistant uses. Leave it blank to use the default. A change takes effect when you press Return or leave the field, and only a change to a different model ends conversations: retyping the current model, or blanking the field while the default is in use, changes nothing. | `claude-opus-5-5` |
13	| **Compact when context reaches … tokens** | When on, a long conversation is replaced by a summary at the end of the first turn that passes the threshold (see [Long conversations](#long-conversations-the-context-meter-and-compaction)). The field accepts 20,000 to 900,000 and is enabled only while the box is checked. | on, 300,000 |
14	| **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** | Lets Anthropic drop old tool results from what the model sees. | off |
15	
16	Under the controls, a status line reports the key's state: "No API key is set." (when neither a saved key nor the environment provides one), "Key saved." or "Key removed.". If the key file cannot be written or removed, the status line shows the file error instead, and nothing changes. Clicking **Save** with an empty field beeps. A threshold outside the range also beeps, and the field goes back to the stored value.
17	
18	**What ends a conversation.** A conversation keeps the key and model it started with. Saving or removing the key, or changing the model to a different one, ends the conversation in every open window. The transcript stays and gets a note: "The API key changed; the next message starts a new conversation." or "The model is now … ; the next message starts a new conversation.". The two chat settings apply without Save and without ending anything. A new compaction threshold applies at the end of the current turn, and a change to clearing applies from the next message.
19	
20	### Where the key is kept
21	
22	A saved key is stored in a file named `anthropic-key` in `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`, which only your user account can read. It goes to the assistant's helper process when a conversation starts and nowhere else. No tool reads or writes the key, the model or the chat settings, so an agent connected over MCP cannot see or change them.
23	
24	If no key is saved, Frame Job uses the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable instead. In practice that only applies when Frame Job is launched from a shell that sets the variable. A saved key always takes precedence.
25	
26	## Opening the Assistant
27	
28	The Assistant is the fifth tab of the inspector, after Clip, Media, Document and Transcript. **View ▸ Assistant** (⌃⌘A) shows the inspector if it was hidden, switches to the Assistant tab and puts the cursor in the message field.
29	
30	From top to bottom, the tab has:
31	
32	1. **Context**: the context meter, with **Clear** (↺, "Clear the conversation") at its right end.
33	2. **Spend**: what this conversation has cost so far.
34	3. **The transcript.**
35	4. **The ask-first row**, shown only while the assistant is waiting for your permission.
36	5. **The message field and Send.**
37	
38	Without a key, the message field is replaced by "Add your Anthropic API key in Settings to use the assistant." and an **Open Settings…** button. **View ▸ Assistant** stays enabled with no key, so the tab can say this; saving the key in Settings brings the message field back at once. If a conversation is started without a key anyway (an agent's `assistant_send`), it fails with "No Anthropic API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant."
39	
40	The tab doesn't switch away on its own while you work in it. The assistant's own edits change the selection without moving you to the Clip tab. Clicking a clip in the timeline or on the canvas still shows the Clip tab, as it always does.
41	
42	## Sending a message
43	
44	Type in the field ("Ask about or edit this project…") and press Return or click **Send**. The field starts one line high and grows to five lines as you type. Past five lines it scrolls.
45	
46	| Key | In the message field |
47	|---|---|
48	| Return or keypad Enter | Sends the message and gives the keys back to the editor, so Space plays while the assistant works. While the assistant is working or waiting for an answer, it beeps instead and the field keeps the keys. |
49	| ⇧Return, ⌘Return, ⌥Return, ⌃Return | Starts a new line |
50	| Tab, ⇧Tab | Gives the keys back to the editor. With Full Keyboard Access on, moves focus to the next or previous control |
51	| ⌘Z, ⇧⌘Z | Undoes or redoes your typing. Typing never lands on the project's undo stack. |
52	
53	The field empties once the message is sent. If the conversation cannot start (for example, the key was removed), the reason appears in red in the transcript and your text stays in the field.
54	
55	While a turn runs, **Send** reads **Stop**. See [Stopping a turn](#stopping-a-turn).
56	
57	### What each message carries
58	
59	Each message you send starts with a short block describing your window at the moment you pressed Send:
60	
61	- the project's name, and its path (or "never saved")
62	- the nest open in the window, if any (otherwise the timeline)
63	- the playhead, in ticks and in seconds
64	- the selected clip ids
65	
66	So "split this clip at the playhead" or "make the selected titles bigger" mean what you'd expect. The block isn't updated during the assistant's turn. After its own edits, the assistant reads the project again.
67	
68	## The transcript
69	
70	The transcript is one block of text. You can select across entries and copy it as plain text. It scrolls to the newest line as the reply arrives.
71	
72	| What you see | Style |
73	|---|---|
74	| Your message | Semibold |
75	| The assistant's reply, streamed as it is written | Regular |
76	| Its working notes between tool calls | Small, faint |
77	| One line per tool call: the tool's name and its arguments, e.g. `split (at: 96000, clips: [12])` (first 70 characters) | Small monospace |
78	| `failed: …` for a tool call that was refused, with the reason | Small monospace |
79	| `Allowed: …` / `Declined: …` for each permission question, or `Declined (stop): …`, `Declined (close): …` or `Declined (helper): …` when it was declined by Stop, by closing the window or by the helper stopping | Small monospace |
80	| Compaction and clearing notes, and notes about key, model or spend-ledger problems | Small monospace |
81	| `Cost: …` at the end of each turn | Small monospace |
82	| Errors | Red |
83	
84	Errors you may see:
85	
86	- "API error *status*: *message*": Anthropic refused or failed the request (a bad key, a rate limit, an outage). Rate limits, outages and connection failures are retried up to three times before this appears. A bad key fails at once.
87	- "The reply was cut off at the output limit."
88	- "The model declined this request."
89	- "The assistant helper stopped. Clear the conversation to start a new one."
90	
91	If the helper stops, a waiting question is declined. Your next message starts a new conversation under the old transcript, and the Spend row carries on from where it was. Click **Clear** to start clean.
92	
93	If a response's cost cannot be written to the spend ledger, the transcript notes it once per conversation: "The spend ledger *path* could not be written: *reason*." That response is then missing from the month's total in Settings.
94	
95	The assistant works for up to 30 rounds of tool calls in one turn, then stops.
96	
97	**Clear** (↺) ends the conversation, empties the transcript and resets the Spend row and the meter. The meter keeps the model's window size, so it reads "0 of *L* tokens · 0%" until the next response. Your next message starts a fresh conversation. Closing the window also ends its conversation. Conversations aren't saved with the project, and each window has its own.
98	
99	## What the assistant can do
100	
101	The assistant has the same tools an agent has over MCP (see [MCP](mcp.md)), with a few exceptions listed below. It can:
102	
103	- open, create and save projects, move the playhead, set the in and out range, change the selection, and enter or leave a nest
104	- add, remove, reorder and set tracks; add and edit markers; change the canvas
105	- import, relink and remove media, copy it into the project (it asks first), and set a media's camera log
106	- place media, text, shapes, backgrounds, adjustment clips and graphics; insert, overwrite, paste and duplicate
107	- move, trim, split, slip, roll, rate-stretch, ripple-delete, lift, insert time and close gaps; detach audio and attach it again, and make J- and L-cuts
108	- nest clips, or take a nest apart
109	- set speed, reverse, freeze frames and add speed ramps (see [Speed](speed.md))
110	- change how a clip looks and sounds, including transitions, actions and zooms; rename a clip, hide or mute it, and paste attributes
111	- import captions, transcribe on this Mac, read a clip's timed words, and export captions
112	- find silences and filler words, normalize loudness and synchronize audio
113	- write, place and change graphics modules; import fonts and assets; rename, delete or restore a module
114	- export, check an export's progress, or cancel it
115	- render a frame of the timeline to look at the result, before and after a visual edit
116	
117	Every edit is one undo step on the project, the same as your own. A turn isn't grouped: each edit is its own step, so a turn that made ten edits takes ten Undos, and **Edit ▸ Undo** names each step after its edit, as it does for an agent's call over MCP. **Edit ▸ Undo** (⌘Z) outside the message field takes back the assistant's last change. You can also ask the assistant to undo.
118	
119	**How it behaves.** Its replies are short, a sentence or two, and don't repeat what the tool lines already show. It writes or restyles captions only when you ask. It renders a frame to look before and after a visual edit. The model runs at medium effort with thinking on, and the faint working notes between tool calls are its thinking updates.
120	
121	The assistant works only on its own window's project. A tool call that names another project is refused.
122	
123	**Cutting words.** Ask it to take out filler words and it finds them and cuts them in one step, but only in media that already have a cloud transcript made with filler words (by **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**). The assistant can't upload audio to make one, so in other media it cuts nothing (the search reports which media have no such transcript). Ask it to remove a false start and it reads the clip's words and their times (from the media's cached transcript, or from this Mac's own speech recogniser, never the network), says which words it will cut, then cuts them as one undo step. It removes a false start only when you ask, because deciding what was a false start is a judgement call. See [Clean-up tools](cleanup-tools.md).
124	
125	### Tools it will not call
126	
127	`record_screen`, `close_project` and `transcribe_for_fillers` are removed from what the assistant can see. `transcribe` stays available for transcribing on this Mac, and only a call with the cloud engine (AssemblyAI) is refused. All four are refused if the assistant calls them anyway, and the call shows in the transcript as a `failed:` line: "*tool* is not available to the assistant: *reason*" (for the cloud case, `transcribe with engine "assemblyai" is not available to the assistant: …`). The reason names the menu item to use instead.
128	
129	| Tool | Why | Do it yourself with |
130	|---|---|---|
131	| `record_screen` | Recording needs a person at the Record button. | **File ▸ New Recording…** (⌥⌘N) |
132	| `close_project` | Closing the project would close the window the conversation lives in. | **File ▸ Close** (⌘W) |
133	| `transcribe` with the cloud engine (AssemblyAI) | Audio leaves the machine only when you choose it, with the price in front of you. | **File ▸ Generate Captions…** |
134	| `transcribe_for_fillers` | The same: it uploads audio to the cloud. | **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…** |
135	
136	### Tools it asks about first
137	
138	Five tools ask first: `export`, `export_captions`, `save_project`, `consolidate_media` and `export_graphic`; a sixth, `new_project_from_range`, asks only when it names a `path` (without one it opens an untitled project and writes no package); and a seventh, `make_vertical_version`, asks only when it names a `path` too. Before each one runs, the tab shows the ask-first row, "The assistant asks first:", with a sentence that says what will happen, and **Allow** and **Deny** buttons:
139	
140	| Tool | The question reads |
141	|---|---|
142	| `export` | "export writes *path*", or "export REPLACES *path*" when a file is already there |
143	| `export_captions` | "export_captions writes *path*" (or REPLACES) |
144	| `save_project` | "save_project writes *path*" (or REPLACES); "save_project writes a file" when no path is known |
145	| `consolidate_media` | "consolidate_media copies every referenced file into *package*/media", or "… into the project's package" when the project has never been saved |
146	| `new_project_from_range` | "new_project_from_range writes *path*", `.framejob` added when missing (only with a `path`) |
147	| `make_vertical_version` | "make_vertical_version writes *path*", `.framejob` added when missing (only with a `path`) |
148	
149	A `~` in the path is expanded before the question is asked, so the sentence shows the full path.
150	
151	Other tools the assistant can call write files without asking: `render_frame` writes a PNG (to a temporary file, or to a path the model names), and `write_graphic`, `import_graphic_font` and `import_graphic_asset` write graphics modules, fonts and assets into the project's package.
152	
153	While a question waits, the **Assistant** tab title shows a small dot, whichever inspector tab you are on. Answer with a click: Return never answers a question. Nothing runs until you click **Allow**. **Deny** tells the assistant you declined, and it won't retry that call in the same turn unless you ask. Stopping the turn, closing the window or the helper stopping each count as a decline. Other windows' assistants and agents over MCP keep working while one window waits for an answer.
154	
155	### While you are dragging
156	
157	If one of the assistant's tool calls arrives while you are in the middle of a drag (on the timeline, the canvas or an inspector slider), it waits until you release the mouse. Then it runs as its own undo step, after yours, so your drag never undoes the assistant's change or mixes with it. The same applies to agents over MCP.
158	
159	The assistant's tool calls and MCP agents' calls take turns, one at a time, and each window's calls run in order. While a window waits for your **Allow** or **Deny**, MCP agents and other windows keep working.
160	
161	### Stopping a turn
162	
163	Click **Stop** (the Send button while a turn runs). Stop:
164	
165	- ends the request to Anthropic
166	- declines a question that is waiting
167	- answers every tool call that has not started yet with "Cancelled by the user."
168	- cancels an on-device transcription or transcript read that is running. Any other tool call that has already started is allowed to finish.
169	
170	An export is handed to the Export Queue as soon as it starts, so Stop doesn't reach it. Cancel it in the Export Queue, or ask the assistant to cancel it. See [Export](export.md).
171	
172	## Long conversations: the context meter and compaction
173	
174	The **Context** meter shows how much of the model's context window the conversation is using, as of the last response:
175	
176	- "Nothing reported yet" before the first response
177	- "*N* of *L* tokens · *P*%" once the model's window is known (shortened to "*N* / *L* · *P*%" or "*P*%" when the inspector is narrow; the tooltip always has the full figure)
178	- "*N* tokens (window size unknown)" if Anthropic did not report the window size
179	
180	The bar under the figure fills in the accent colour and turns red past 80%.
181	
182	**Compaction.** With **Compact when context reaches** on, the conversation is summarised at the end of the first turn that passes the threshold, never in the middle of a turn. The summary keeps what you asked for and your stated preferences, the project and the clips, tracks, markers and media involved, the edits made and undone, and what is still open. The transcript notes "Compacting the conversation (*N* tokens)…" and then "Compacted: *N* → about *M* tokens. Earlier renders are gone; the assistant re-renders when it needs to look.". If no summary comes back, the note says compaction didn't finish and that it will try again after the next turn. The summary request is priced like any other response.
183	
184	With compaction off, a conversation grows until it fills the model's window, and requests then fail until you click **Clear**.
185	
186	**Clearing old tool results.** With **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** on, Anthropic may drop older tool results from what the model sees once the conversation passes 150,000 tokens. It keeps the five most recent, clears at least 50,000 tokens at a time, and can happen mid-turn. Each clearing adds a note, "Cleared *N* old tool results (*M* tokens) from the model's view.", and costs a fresh prompt-cache write. The model may have to fetch something again after a clearing.
187	
188	## What it costs
189	
190	Every response is priced by Frame Job from LiteLLM's published Anthropic prices. All the figures below are **Frame Job's own estimate**. The Anthropic Console shows what your account was actually billed.
191	
192	### Per turn
193	
194	Each turn ends with a line in the transcript:
195	
196	`Cost: $0.0182 · Frame Job's estimate at LiteLLM prices (cached 2026-10-25)`
197	
198	The part in brackets names the price table and its date: "bundled table of …" (the copy built into the app), "cached …" or "fetched …" (a copy Frame Job refreshes at most once a day). If a refresh failed, the line adds "not refreshed:" and the reason.
199	
200	- A response that could not be priced shows as "unknown (*reason*)", never $0, followed by "at least" the part that could be priced.
201	- A response cut short by Stop or an error is priced from what had arrived, as "at least $… (a response was cut short)".
202	- Amounts are shown to four decimal places. A tiny positive amount reads "under $0.0001".
203	
204	### Per conversation
205	
206	The tab's **Spend** row adds up the conversation's turns since the last **Clear**, or since a key or model change ended the conversation:
207	
208	- "Nothing yet" before the first response
209	- "$0.0532 · Frame Job's estimate"
210	- "at least $… · Frame Job's estimate" when a response was cut short or could not be priced (shortened to "≥$…" when narrow)
211	- "under $0.0001 · Frame Job's estimate" for a tiny positive amount (shortened to "<$0.0001" when narrow)
212	- "unknown · Frame Job's estimate" when nothing could be priced
213	
214	Hovering the figure shows "What this conversation's responses cost at LiteLLM prices, as Frame Job estimates it. The Anthropic Console shows what your account was billed."
215	
216	### Per month
217	
218	Under the buttons in **Settings ▸ Assistant**, a line totals the current calendar month in UTC, for example "October 2026 (UTC): $1.24 over 87 responses.". Variants report "Nothing recorded in …", responses that could not be priced, and ledger lines that could not be read. Totals are rounded to the cent, and a tiny positive amount reads "under $0.01". While the ledger is being read the line says "Reading the spend ledger…", and if it cannot be read, "The spend ledger could not be read: *reason*.". The line refreshes when Settings opens and after each response while Settings is visible. Under it, a faint note says: "Frame Job's own estimate at LiteLLM prices, from its spend ledger. The Anthropic Console shows what your account was billed."
219	
220	The figures come from a spend ledger, `spend.jsonl` in `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`, with one line per response: the time, the model, the token counts and the dollars. It never records your key or the conversation's content.
221	
222	## Privacy: what leaves your Mac
223	
224	When you use the assistant, these go to Anthropic, under your key:
225	
226	- your messages, and the context block in front of each one (the project's name and path, the open nest, the playhead, the selection)
227	- what the tools answer: the project's details as JSON (including media file paths), clip transcripts it reads, refusals and other results
228	- the frames it renders to look at the picture
229	
230	Frame Job doesn't send any of this anywhere else. Audio never goes to the cloud transcriber from the assistant (see [Tools it will not call](#tools-it-will-not-call)). The assistant asks before it exports a movie or captions, saves the project, or consolidates media; other tools can still write files without asking (a rendered frame's PNG, and graphics modules, fonts and assets in the project's package). Once a day at most, the helper downloads LiteLLM's public price table from GitHub. That request carries no key and no project data.
231	
232	Everything else stays on your Mac: the key file, the spend ledger and the cached price table, `anthropic-prices.json`, all in `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`. The conversation itself is kept in memory only, and goes when you clear it or close the window.
233	
234	## Limits
235	
236	- The assistant works only on the project in its own window, and each window has its own conversation.
237	- It needs your own Anthropic API key. There is no Frame Job account or relay.
238	- It can't record the screen, close its window's project, or send audio to the cloud transcriber.
239	- A tool call that arrives during a drag waits until you release the mouse.
240	- Stop doesn't cancel an export that has already been queued.
241	- With compaction off, a long conversation eventually fails until you **Clear** it.
242	- Changing the key or the model ends every window's conversation.
243	
244	*Agents:* none. The Assistant is the person's own conversation, and its settings are deliberately out of reach of any tool. An agent drives the same tools directly over [MCP](mcp.md), and is never asked first or refused by the assistant's rules above.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library

  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a

  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,

  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,

  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil

  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell

  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS

  `add_adjustment_clip`, sent scoped) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and

  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `VideoProps.swift` · `ClipSnapshot.swift` ·

  and format 31's `AudioProps.isolation` (AU-50), and format 32's `eq`, `hum` and `channels`

  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-43, AU-45), and format 34's `voice`
  (`VoiceProps.swift`, AU-140), and format 37's `leveller`

  `ClipSnapshot.swift`'s `TransitionSnapshot.audioShape` is `plus_3db` when absent, and

  creator-jobs CU3a1, spec §11 CU-30, CU-39) holds `CursorStyle`, `CursorClicks` (`off` is the
  core's `none`: a case named `none` warns), `CursorProps` (`VideoProps.cursor` and
  `VideoPatch.cursor`; its `dictionary` writes all eight keys, `NSNull` for a nil `hideIdle`),
  `CursorPatch` (all eight keys, the sparse write `VideoPatch.cursorPart` carries — written
  under `cursor` only when `cursor` is nil, never decoded, `cutoutPart`'s shape — so each Cursor

  `MediaCursor` (`MediaSnapshot.cursor`, `MediaDescriptor.cursor`, kept by `probeDictionary`) and

**The document.**
- `ProjectDocument.swift` (+`DisplayStem`, +`Recording`, +`SelectedAction`, +`Import`, +`Graphics`, +`GraphicFiles`, +`UndoGroup`, +`CacheSaves`, +`Alerts`, +`Reverse`, +`Derived`)

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

3	/// Where a session is: `closed` > `asking` > `busy` > `idle`, the first that
4	/// holds. Main only.
5	enum AssistantPhase: String {
6	    case idle, busy, asking, closed
7	}
8	
9	/// Why a session could not be opened, in the sentence a caller shows as is.
10	struct AssistantOpenError: Error {
11	    let message: String
12	}
